title: ⚛️ useState vs useRef — What's the Difference in React?
excerpt: Two commonly used React Hooks are useState and useRef.
body:
ㅤ
📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 13
ㅤ
When building React applications, we often need to store and manage values.

Two commonly used React Hooks are useState and useRef.

Both can preserve values between renders, but they behave differently.

Let's understand with simple examples! 👇
ㅤ
1️⃣ 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 — 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗨𝗜 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 🔄

useState stores values that affect what users see on the screen.

When we update state using its setter, React schedules a re-render.

Example:

const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

<button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>
  Count: {count}
</button>

Every button click updates the count displayed on the screen.

✅ Stores component state
✅ Triggers UI updates
✅ Useful for counters, forms, and toggles
ㅤ
2️⃣ 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗥𝗲𝗳 — 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲𝘀 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗥𝗲-𝗥𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 📦

useRef stores a mutable value that persists between renders.

Unlike useState, changing ref.current does not trigger a re-render.

Example:

const countRef = useRef(0);

function handleClick() {
  countRef.current += 1;
  console.log(countRef.current);
}

The value increases with every click, but React doesn't re-render because the ref changed.

✅ Preserves values between renders
✅ Does not trigger re-renders
✅ Useful for timers and DOM references
ㅤ
3️⃣ 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 — 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻 𝗜𝗻𝗽𝘂𝘁 🎯

Imagine clicking a button to focus a search field.

const inputRef = useRef(null);

function focusInput() {
  inputRef.current?.focus();
}

<input ref={inputRef} />
<button onClick={focusInput}>Focus</button>

Here, useRef gives us access to the input element without needing state.
ㅤ
4️⃣ 𝗤𝘂𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗻 ⚖️

🔹 useState
• Stores UI-related state
• Updates trigger re-renders
• Read the value during rendering

🔹 useRef
• Stores mutable references
• Updates don't trigger re-renders
• Access values using .current
ㅤ
💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

Use useState when changing a value should update the UI.

Use useRef when you need to remember a value without triggering a re-render.

Choosing the right Hook helps keep React components clean and predictable.

🚀 Understanding when to use each is more important than simply knowing their syntax.
ㅤ
